t: Knowledge Source Prioritizer - Signature build-tool concept
title: Knowledge Source Prioritizer - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Ranks sources using explicit trust, relevance, and freshness criteria.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through Knowledge Source Prioritizer: Ranks sources using explicit trust, relevance, and freshness criteria. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats Knowledge Source Prioritizer as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the Knowledge Source Prioritizer produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the Knowledge Source Prioritizer is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Chunker - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
title: Signature Chunker - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
definition: The Chunker component of the Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework, owning chunker. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework decomposes the capability (Ranks sources using explicit trust, relevance, and freshness criteria.) into seven pillars, and the Chunker is the one that owns the framework's chunker responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Knowledge Source Prioritizer result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Chunker's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Chunker's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Knowledge Source Prioritizer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Embedder - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
title: Signature Embedder - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
definition: The Embedder component of the Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework, owning embedder. Signature concept.
description:
The Embedder is a load-bearing component of the Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's embedder responsibilities belongs to the Embedder, and the Embedder answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Embedder can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Embedder works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Knowledge Source Prioritizer charter (ranks sources using explicit trust, relevance, and freshness criteria.). The Embedder reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small rag job that needs Knowledge Source Prioritizer. The Embedder takes the request's embedder responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Embedder's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Retriever - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
title: Signature Retriever - Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework pillar
definition: The Retriever component of the Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework, owning retriever. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Knowledge Source Prioritizer framework, the Retriever owns the framework's retriever responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Retriever's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Retriever from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Ranks sources using explicit trust, relevance, and freshness criteria.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Retrieval-augmented generation and grounded answers build needs Knowledge Source Prioritizer, so the framework invokes the Retriever on the the framework's retriever responsibilities portion of the work. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.
